q: The magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through that loop.
e: True. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through that loop.

q: In Faraday's law equation, the minus sign gives the magnitude of the induced emf.
e: False. The right claim is this: In Faraday's law equation, the minus sign gives the direction of the induced emf. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. The printed line wrongly says in Faraday's law equation, the minus sign gives the magnitude of the induced emf.

q: If the wire loop is moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is no induced emf.
e: True. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is no induced emf.

q: Faraday's law gives the magnitude of the induced emf and Lenz's law gives its direction.
e: True. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Faraday is the name attached to this result.

q: An induced emf is always in a direction that aids the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it.
e: False. The right claim is this: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. The printed line wrongly says an induced emf is always in a direction that aids the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it.

q: Lenz's law is a good example of the principle of conservation of energy.
e: True. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it. Lenz is the name attached to this result.

q: Lenz's law shows how the energy from the mechanical work done against the opposing force is transformed into electrical energy.
e: True. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it. Lenz is the name attached to this result. Lenz is the name attached to this result.

q: When a magnet is moved towards a coil, the induced current in the coil produces a magnetic field that attracts the magnet.
e: False. The right claim is this: When a magnet is moved towards a coil, the magnetic flux through the coil increases, and the induced current must produce a magnetic field which opposes an increase in the original magnetic flux. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The printed line wrongly says when a magnet is moved towards a coil, the induced current in the coil produces a magnetic field that attracts the magnet.
